title: What we will build and learn
summary: The customer problem, the finished application and the Azure skills you will practise.
text:
A product retailer has manuals that customers and support staff must search for answers. We will deploy an assistant that answers questions from those manuals. 
 Customer benefit 
 The goal is less time searching documents and fewer repetitive support questions. Answers include the supporting manual passages, so users can check specifications and instructions. When the manuals cannot answer a question, the assistant says so. 
  Example:  “Does the Harbor Travel Kettle work on 110 V?” The assistant points to the manual's 220–240 V requirement rather than guessing. 
 What we will do 
  Deploy the supplied Java and Python applications and their Azure services.  Upload fictional product manuals and watch them become searchable.  Ask product questions, inspect cited answers and test an unsupported question.  Observe queue-driven scaling, run the deployment smoke test and clean up.  
 All application code is supplied. Your work is mainly to build, configure, deploy and inspect it. 
 What you will learn 
   Containers:  build, tag and push Docker images; deploy and inspect AKS Pods, Services, probes, logs and rollouts.   Events:  connect Blob uploads through Event Grid to a small Python Function; distinguish notifications from queued work.   Data and RAG:  apply Flyway migrations, chunk manuals, create embeddings and retrieve filtered evidence with PostgreSQL/pgvector.   Asynchronous chat:  use Service Bus request/reply, persistent state, correlation IDs and retry-safe processing.   Identity and configuration:  use managed/workload identity, Key Vault secrets and App Configuration settings.   Operations:  observe KEDA scale workers from zero, diagnose failures and verify cleanup.  
 Before you start 
   Azure:  an active subscription, resource/role-assignment permissions, and model/VM quota.   Local:  Azure CLI, Bicep, Docker, kubectl, Java 21, Python 3.12+ and Git. On Windows, use Ubuntu in WSL2 with Docker Desktop integration.  
 Use the  prerequisite checklist  and  setup downloads . Allow about four hours  after  setup; this estimate has not been timed. 
  Applications and source code 
    Application / source repo  Responsibility       Products   Java 21 / Spring Boot on AKS. Server-rendered upload/chat UI; JDBC, PostgreSQL and Flyway. Always at least one replica.     ProductsEmbedder   Python Function. Reads uploaded manuals, creates chunks/embeddings and stores them in pgvector.     ProductsChat   Python worker on AKS. Retrieves chunks, calls the chat model and replies through Service Bus. KEDA scales it from zero.    
 
  Upload and indexing flow 
   Products Commit product + manual ID  →   Private blob Upload .txt  →   Event Grid → Function Read, chunk, embed  →   PostgreSQL Store vectors; mark ready  Upload success precedes indexing completion. Event Grid carries a notification; the Function reads the blob separately.  
 
  Question and answer flow 
   Products + DB Persist question + outbox  →   Request queue Service Bus  →   Chat worker Embed → retrieve → generate  →   Reply queue → Products Persist answer; browser polls  Persistent request/correlation IDs connect the flow. Embeddings find evidence; the LLM generates the answer.  
 
 Selected  AI-200 objectives . Use the shared term tooltips for definitions;  reference notes  cover costs and design tradeoffs. 
  Verification:  identify the customer problem and the upload → indexing → cited-answer flow, then check prerequisites.

title: Check your starting point
summary: Check tools, Azure permissions, regional capacity and model access.
text:
Required before the workshop 
   Account:  an active Azure subscription with billing/credits. Plan roughly US$5–15 for a four-hour run and prompt cleanup; see  cost assumptions .   Permissions:  subscription Owner, or Contributor + Role Based Access Control Administrator. Organizational policy can still restrict deployments.   Capacity:  regional services, eight free vCPUs for the selected VM family/region (node + upgrade surge), and chat/embedding model quota. The checker verifies these; actual model access is tested before AKS creation.   Computer:  package-download access and a Linux-container Docker engine. Windows setup below targets x64 Windows 11 with virtualization/admin access; recommend 16 GB RAM and 30 GB free disk.  
 Local tools 
 Run workshop commands in  Bash from the repository root . Windows tools installed outside WSL do not replace Linux tools. 
    Tool  Baseline      Azure CLI / Bicep  CLI 2.91+ / Bicep 0.49.2    Docker  Engine 24+ with BuildKit; running in Linux-container mode    Java / Python  Java 21; Python 3.12+ with venv/pip    kubectl  Installer uses 1.34.1; stay within one minor of AKS    Utilities  Bash 4+, Git, jq 1.6+, curl, OpenSSL 3, zip/unzip    
 No existing AKS cluster, local PostgreSQL, Helm or Functions host is needed. 
 Setup downloads 
  Windows setup (.ps1)  ·  Ubuntu tools (.sh) . Windows uses Docker Desktop + WSL2; native Linux can use Docker Engine. These scripts install local software only. 
  Windows / Ubuntu installation steps 
  Review   setup-windows.ps1  . In Administrator PowerShell, open its download folder and run below. Add  -WhatIf  to preview. Install  App Installer  if WinGet is missing.  
   PowerShell · Windows Downloads folder  Copy    powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\setup-windows.ps1
    Canonical commands:   setup-windows.ps1   
  Restart if requested, then rerun. Open Ubuntu 24.04 and create its Linux user.  wsl --list --verbose  should show version 2.  Start Docker Desktop; choose WSL2/Linux containers and enable  Settings → Resources → WSL Integration → Ubuntu-24.04 . Review  Docker's license requirements ; WinGet accepts package/source agreements.  Copy/extract the repository into Ubuntu, e.g.  ~/ai200 . In that repository root, run:  
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/setup-ubuntu.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 The Ubuntu script installs the listed tools and  workshop/.tools/venv . No second Docker daemon is installed. See   setup-ubuntu.sh   or the  official installation links  for other systems. 
 
 Already set up? Check local tools without Azure sign-in: 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    python3 workshop/tools/preflight.py --local-only
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Sign in and check Azure 
 Clone the three application repos into sibling folders (or set  AI200_APPS_DIR  to their parent). Existing checkouts are preserved: 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/get-apps.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Run  az login , deliberately select your development subscription with  az account set --subscription SUBSCRIPTION_ID , then confirm  az account show . 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    python3 workshop/tools/bootstrap.py
bash workshop/scripts/00-check.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Review  workshop/.state/config.json . Use a distinct  --prefix  per participant in a shared subscription, before provisioning. 
  Bootstrap defaults and overrides  Bootstrap saves non-secret config in  workshop/.state/config.json : Sweden Central, prefix  raglab , selected subscription and your public IPv4 /32. Review it. Shared subscription? Give each participant a different  --prefix . Other overrides:   bootstrap.py  .  
  Checker failures and provider registration 
 If providers are unregistered, register them and rerun the checks: 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/00-check.sh --register
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
   Missing quota/model offers:  register providers first; empty API results do not prove capacity. Check Subscription → Usage + quotas or change region.   Permission denied:  obtain the subscription roles listed above; check deny policies.   Docker unavailable:  start Desktop and enable Ubuntu integration.   Java mismatch:  select Java 21 through  JAVA_HOME / PATH  in Bash.  
 Keep the same prefix/subscription after provisioning; change a colliding name before creation. If your VPN/public IP changes, update the exact allowed /32. 
 
 Prepare verification tools 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    python3 -m venv workshop/.tools/venv
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source workshop/.tools/venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r workshop/requirements-test.txt
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Resume this environment with  source workshop/.tools/venv/bin/activate . 
  Verification:  the full checker reports "All read-only gates passed." No paid resources have been created. Continue to provisioning.

title: Start the Azure resources
summary: Test model access, then provision Azure while you build locally.
text:
Requires:  prerequisite checks pass; subscription, region and source IP reviewed.  
 Cost check 
 This creates paid resources. Allow roughly  US$5–15  for four hours with prompt cleanup (11 November 2026 estimate, not a measured bill). VM, PostgreSQL, NAT and service tiers continue billing while the worker is idle.  Cost details . 
 Start provisioning 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/01-models.sh
bash workshop/scripts/02-provision.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
   01 → models:  creates the tagged resource group and model deployments, then makes identity-based embedding/chat calls. AKS/database creation waits for this gate.   02 → infrastructure:  creates networking, ACR, Storage, queues, Key Vault, App Configuration, identities and telemetry; starts PostgreSQL and AKS/Functions deployments asynchronously.  
 Defaults:  gpt-5-mini  +  text-embedding-3-small , 1536 dimensions, PostgreSQL 17, one AKS node, Python 3.12 Functions Flex. Passwords go into Key Vault; never enable  set -x . 
  Networking and infrastructure sources 
    Traffic  Connection      AKS / Function → PostgreSQL  Private VNet + private DNS; no public database firewall rule    Workloads → Azure services  Public TLS endpoints, Entra identity, explicit NAT egress    Event Grid → Function  HTTPS Blob-extension webhook + system key    Browser → Products  Public HTTPS, source IPv4 /32 restriction and sign-in; private blobs    
 Templates:   models.bicep  ,   foundation.bicep  ,   database.bicep  ,   compute.bicep  . Separate delegated subnets provide Functions/DB integration. GlobalStandard model processing may occur outside the account region. 
 
 Build while Azure runs 
 Continue directly to Products. Stage 03 later checks readiness, with bounded waits and failed-operation diagnostics. Accepted deployments are not yet ready. 
  Verification:  the model probe passes and the script reports AKS/Functions and PostgreSQL provisioning. These are expected results;  observed validation  is recorded separately. 
  Troubleshooting    Model probe fails:  fix model access/quota/region before starting compute.   ARM failure:  inspect the reported operation for policy, SKU or regional restrictions.   Name reserved/soft-deleted:  recover your own resource or use a new prefix; do not adopt another group's resources.   Interrupted:  rerun the same stage/config. Scripts reuse matching resources and reject a group with another workshop tag.

title: Read, build and run Products
summary: Build, tag, push and run the supplied Java/Python images.
text:
Requires:  stage 02 submitted, ACR created and Docker running. Azure can still be provisioning.  
  Application source walkthrough 
    ProductsController.java  : validate UTF-8 .txt, commit product/manual IDs, upload the private blob.    Store.java   +   MessagePump.java  : explicit SQL, persistent chat/outbox and reply handling.  Thymeleaf templates +   app.js  : server-rendered forms and browser polling.  
 
  Dockerfile and container basics 
 An image packages the application; a container runs it. The build stage uses Maven/Java 21; the runtime copies only the JAR and runs unprivileged.  EXPOSE  documents a port;  docker run -p  publishes it. 
   Dockerfile   is maintained in the Products repository. 
 
 Build, tag and push 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/05-images.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
   05-images.sh   builds both images for  linux/amd64 , logs into ACR, assigns content-derived  w1-…  tags with  -t , and pushes. Products uses its app folder as build context; the worker uses the repository root for shared Python code. State/secrets are excluded. 
 Run locally 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    tag=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("workshop/.state/images.json"))["tag"])')
registry=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("workshop/.state/config.json"))["stem"]+"acr.azurecr.io")')
docker run --rm --name products-inspect -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 \
  "$registry/products:$tag" --spring.profiles.active=inspect
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 In another Bash terminal: 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8080/
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/liveness
docker ps
docker logs products-inspect --tail=30
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Expect  Inspect profile  and health  UP . This profile has no upload/chat or Azure connections. Stop the container with Ctrl+C. 
  Exercise: tag the same image / build Java locally  Using the run block's variables, execute  docker tag "$registry/products:$tag" products-local:$tag , then  docker image inspect "products-local:$tag" . Both references identify the same image; a tag can move, a digest identifies content.  For a local Java build: in the sibling  ai200-workshop1-products  checkout, run  bash mvnw test  with Java 21. Integration tests need the  database fixture .  
  Verification:  both pushes return digests and localhost health is UP. Continue to data/identity setup. 
  Troubleshooting    Push denied:  check subscription/push rights and rerun the stage's ACR login.   Port busy:  map  127.0.0.1:8081:8080  and use 8081 locally.   Download failure:  check Docker's network/proxy and rerun; completed layers are cached.   Exec format error:  use the supplied  linux/amd64  platform.

title: Connect data, settings and identity
summary: Connect PostgreSQL, storage, configuration and identities.
text:
Requires:  stages 01–02 submitted and images pushed.  
 Wait, then configure 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/03-ready.sh
bash workshop/scripts/04-configure.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
  03-ready.sh  waits for ARM, a Ready node and the PostgreSQL  VECTOR  allowlist.  04-configure.sh  assigns roles, federation, kubelet AcrPull, KEDA's separate identity and ordinary settings. 
  How identity, settings and secrets connect 
   AKS service account Client-ID annotation + Pod label  →   Federation OIDC → Entra token  →   App Configuration Endpoints and settings  →   Key Vault Read passwords  Functions uses managed identity directly. All apps read settings/secrets at startup; changes require restart.  
    Mechanism  Workshop use      Key Vault  PostgreSQL and Products sign-in passwords    App Configuration  Endpoints, model names, retrieval count, chunk size    ConfigMap  Non-secret App Configuration endpoint/label    Kubernetes Secret  Endpoint TLS certificate/private key    Environment variables  Bootstrap settings and SDK identity metadata    Managed/workload identity  Short-lived tokens; Azure roles grant access separately    
 Bootstrap and federation  Applications start with  APP_CONFIG_ENDPOINT  and label  workshop . App Configuration provides service settings and the vault URI; Key Vault supplies passwords. AKS requires the service-account annotation  azure.workload.identity/client-id , Pod label  azure.workload.identity/use: "true"  and a federated credential matching issuer/subject/audience. See   products.yaml   and   04-configure.sh  . 
 
 Inspect the Flyway migration 
   V1__products_and_messages.sql   creates the schema when Products starts. Flyway records versions/checksums; reruns validate existing migrations. 
  Schema and upload consistency 
  Both document/question embeddings use the same deployment and  vector(1536) . Retrieval uses exact cosine distance  <=> ; no ANN index.  Chunk key:  (manual_id, chunk_index) . Chunks + ready state commit atomically.  Question + outbox commit together; replies/results persist by request ID.  
 The product row commits  before  blob upload. Failed uploads persist failure; abandoned waiting work times out. Manuals are immutable. 
 
  Database simplification  The workshop shares the  workshopadmin  database owner across migrations/apps, with its password in Key Vault. Production should separate runtime/migration roles. Private DNS/VNet access keeps PostgreSQL private; your laptop normally cannot connect directly.  
  Verification:  node Ready, VECTOR allowlisted, settings/roles configured. Flyway runs in the next chapter. 
  Troubleshooting    Database DNS/connectivity:  check the private zone's VNet link and delegated subnet; do not open an internet-wide firewall rule.   Vault/settings 403:  check workload principal, role scope and propagation; CLI sign-in does not configure the Pod.   Extension failure:  allowlist VECTOR; create SQL extension  vector  as the database owner.   KEDA authentication:  inspect its own identity/federation, independently of the worker.

title: Deploy Products to AKS
summary: Deploy Products; inspect probes, logs and a rollout.
text:
Requires:  stages 03–05 pass; images are in ACR.  
  Deployment, Service and probe basics 
    products.yaml  : Deployment keeps one Java Pod running; service account + Pod labels enable identity. Startup permits initialization; readiness checks the database; liveness checks the process.    service.yaml  : LoadBalancer Service selects ready Products Pods and forwards 443 → 8443. Access is restricted to your public IPv4 /32.  
 
 Deploy and sign in 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/06-products.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 The stage creates the Service, waits for an IP, installs a TLS Secret and deploys Products. Open the printed URL; username  participant , password from  bash workshop/scripts/credentials.sh  in your terminal. 
  TLS:  the two-day certificate is self-signed. Compare the printed SHA-256 fingerprint before accepting the browser warning. CLI tools trust  workshop/.state/tls.crt . 
 Inspect and restart 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    export KUBECONFIG="$PWD/workshop/.state/kubeconfig"
kubectl get deployment,pods,service -n products
kubectl logs deployment/products -n products --tail=50
kubectl describe pod -n products -l app=products
kubectl rollout restart deployment/products -n products
kubectl rollout status deployment/products -n products --timeout=300s
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Find one ready Pod, the load-balancer IP, Flyway startup/validation and probe settings. The restart replaces the Pod and reuses the database schema. 
  Verification:  sign in and open both upload/chat views; the restarted deployment becomes Ready.  Wait until the next chapter's Function subscription is ready before uploading.  Earlier BlobCreated events are not replayed automatically. 
  Troubleshooting    ImagePullBackOff:  describe the Pod; verify the pushed tag and kubelet AcrPull role.   CrashLoopBackOff:  inspect  kubectl logs -n products deployment/products --previous ; check settings, vault and private DB access.   Endpoint blocked:  check VPN/public IP against  allowedCidr ; update the exact /32 and rerun stage 06.   Expired certificate:  rerun stage 06, restart Products and check the new fingerprint.   Write API 403:  use the UI or obtain CSRF/session state from  /api/csrf , as the supplied clients do.

title: Turn a manual into vectors
summary: Trigger Python indexing from a Blob upload; verify stored chunks.
text:
Requires:  Products ready, Flyway applied and model probe passed.  
  How the Event Grid Blob trigger works 
   function_app.py   declares a Blob trigger with  source='EventGrid' . A BlobCreated notification reaches the Blob-extension webhook; the extension reads the private blob and passes an InputStream to Python. The path carries product/manual IDs. 
 
 Publish 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/07-embedder.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 The stage builds the Python package remotely on Linux, publishes it, then registers the filtered Event Grid subscription. Flex Consumption supplies server-managed execution; the template supplies VNet access, identity-based host/deployment storage and telemetry. 
 Upload all three manuals 
    Product name  Download      Aurora Trail Lamp   aurora-trail-lamp.txt     Cedar Desk Fan   cedar-desk-fan.txt     Harbor Travel Kettle   harbor-travel-kettle.txt     
 In Products → Upload product, submit each name/file. Expect  waiting → processing → ready ; intermediate states may be brief. Upload completion is not indexing completion. 
 Inspect stored data 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/inspect-data.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
  Verification:  all three manuals are ready, chunk counts are positive and min/max dimensions equal 1536. The inspection Job runs inside the VNet; it does not print full vectors. 
 Make two changes 
  Copy Aurora's manual, change  420 lumens  to  510 lumens , and label it revision B. Upload as a new product, "Aurora Trail Lamp Rev B". Compare each product's answer in the next chapter.  Activate the verification environment, run  python workshop/tools/replay_event.py , then inspect counts again. Replaying a ready manual twice should add no chunks.  
  Chunking and retry safety    chunks.py   splits at text boundaries with bounded character counts/overlap.   models.py   requests 1536-value embeddings.   embedding.py   locks per manual, checks IDs/checksum, persists processing, then commits chunks + ready atomically.  A ready manual skips indexing. Duplicate Blob receipts may be suppressed before code runs; the database guard also prevents duplicates. Failed attempts persist errors and retry. Delivery is at-least-once; manuals are immutable.  
  Troubleshooting    Still waiting:  check subscription/filter and IndexManual discovery. For uploads made before subscription creation, upload a new product.   No Function/key:  check remote-build logs, extension bundle and host-storage roles: Blob Data Owner, Queue Data Contributor, Storage Account Contributor.   Indexing failed:  use the manual ID in Application Insights; check DB DNS, model identity/quota and dimensions.   Delivery exhausted:  inspect Event Grid's  event-deadletters  blobs separately from the Function host's  webjobs-blobtrigger-poison  queue.

title: Ask a grounded question
summary: Retrieve evidence, generate a cited answer and inspect asynchronous replies.
text:
Requires:  Products ready and the three manuals indexed.  
 Deploy one worker 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/08-chat.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Starts one worker from   chat.yaml  .   worker.py   receives Service Bus requests serially, with prefetch zero. KEDA takes over next. 
 Ask and inspect the evidence 
 In Products → Chat, select the matching product. Compare returned passages, not exact LLM wording. 
    Product / question  Expected evidence      Aurora: operating temperature?  -10 to 40 degrees Celsius    Cedar: how to enable the timer?  Hold two seconds; runs for 45 minutes    Harbor: does it work on 110 V?  220–240 V only; not dual voltage    Any: what is the CEO's private telephone number?  Insufficient information    
 For Aurora revision B, compare lumens using each product filter. Questions and supporting passages:   questions.json  . 
  How retrieval and prompting work 
   chat.py   embeds the question, filters ready chunks by optional product ID, ranks cosine distance with  <=> , and supplies the best passages to the chat model. No useful evidence means an insufficient-information answer. 
 Manuals are untrusted reference data, separated from application instructions. The model receives context, not secrets or tools; citations let you inspect support. 
 
 Change retrieval count 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/change-retrieval.sh 1
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Changes App Configuration from 3 passages to 1 and restarts the worker.  No live refresh.  Ask a new question: startup logs should show  retrieval_count=1 , with at most one source. Existing answers remain cached. Restore with  bash workshop/scripts/change-retrieval.sh 3 . 
  Verification:  observe queued/processing/completed states, cited answers and an unsupported-question refusal. Refreshing the request URL returns the same persisted answer. 
  Request/reply and retry guarantees  Products commits question + outbox, returns HTTP 202, and sends to  chat-requests . The worker validates stored request/correlation IDs, caches the result before sending to  chat-replies , then acknowledges. Products persists the correlated reply before acknowledging it; the browser polls by request ID.  A receive locks work; Complete acknowledges, Abandon retries. Initial lock: one minute; automatic renewal: up to ten minutes; application deadline: eight minutes. Persistent failure/timeouts end browser polling. Repeated failures reach the dead-letter queue.  Advisory locks, cached results and guarded updates prevent duplicate displayed answers. A crash before caching can repeat a paid model call; delivery is not exactly-once. Contracts:   chat-request.schema.json  ,   chat-reply.schema.json  .  
  Troubleshooting    Queued:  check Products' outbox logs, queue counts, worker readiness and Sender/Receiver roles.   Failed/timeout:  inspect worker logs by request ID; check model quota/429s, deployments, DB access and lock renewal.   Wrong product:  compare selected product and returned source IDs. Only unfiltered questions may mix manuals.

title: Make the queue drive scaling
summary: Scale the worker from zero with a bounded queue backlog.
text:
Requires:  chat works, demo tools are installed and all manuals are ready.  
 Enable queue-driven scaling 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/09-keda.sh
bash workshop/scripts/demo-scaling.sh start
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 KEDA scales ProductsChat from zero to three workers. Products stays at one. 
 The demo temporarily adds a  20-second delay per request  to make backlog visible. Normal operation has no delay. 
 Terminal A: observe 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/watch-scaling.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Wait for chat to reach zero; Products stays at one. The observer shows replicas and active/dead-letter counts for up to eight minutes. 
 Terminal B: send eight questions 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
source workshop/.tools/venv/bin/activate
python workshop/tools/load.py --count 8
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 This submits eight persistent questions and waits for their answers (hard maximum twelve). Each normally incurs one embedding + one chat call. 
  Observe:  idle 0 → queued messages → worker starts → more than one worker → completed answers → cooldown back to 0. Management metrics can lag; record actual replicas/timing. 
 Compare threshold 4, then reset 
 After the first cycle returns to idle: 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/demo-scaling.sh threshold 4
python workshop/tools/load.py --count 8
bash workshop/scripts/demo-scaling.sh stop
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Targeting four messages per worker should scale less aggressively under similar backlog. The final command restores normal settings and disables the delay. 
  Verification:  both cycles complete, the first exceeds one worker, no new dead letters, and chat returns to zero. Products stays at one; demo delay is off. 
  What affects scaling?    keda.yaml   scales only ProductsChat:  0–3 replicas , two active messages per worker, 10-second polling, 60-second cooldown. KEDA reads metrics; workers process messages. Its scaler uses a separate identity.  Queue depth drives desired replicas; worker concurrency is one and prefetch zero. Model quota can throttle extra workers. Polling, cold starts, cooldown and HPA stabilization affect timing.  The single D4ds_v5 node has four vCPUs/16 GiB before reservations. Products requests 500m/768 MiB; each worker 250m/384 MiB. Maximum three workers fits without node autoscaling.  
  Troubleshooting    ScaledObject not Ready / 403:  inspect its conditions and  kube-system/keda-operator  logs; check the scaler's federation/Receiver role, not only the worker's.   Only one worker:  confirm delay=20, threshold=2 and prefetch=0; inspect HPA metrics. Repeat bounded load only after diagnosis.   Never zero:  check backlog, cooldown/stabilization and competing manual scaling.   Pending / model 429:  inspect Pod capacity or reduce max replicas/load; more replicas cannot overcome model quota.

title: Verify, diagnose and clean up
summary: Smoke-test the deployment, diagnose failures and remove resources.
text:
Requires:  all components ready, manuals indexed, KEDA Ready and demo delay disabled.  
 Run the deployment smoke test 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
source workshop/.tools/venv/bin/activate
python workshop/tools/smoke.py
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 Checks dependency readiness, uploads Aurora, waits for indexing, submits a temperature question and validates correlation + source evidence. Timeouts: seven minutes for indexing, eight for the reply. Results:  workshop/.state/smoke-result.json . 
  Verification:  smoke passes with a non-empty answer and the matching temperature passage/product/manual IDs. Exact model wording is not asserted.  Maintainer validation  records which checks actually ran. 
 If something fails 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/diagnostics.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
  Troubleshooting by boundary 
    Symptom  Check / fix      Upload failed  Products logs and Blob role/endpoint; retry as a new product after fixing    Manual waiting  Event filter, webhook and Function discovery; pre-subscription uploads need replay/new product    Indexing failed  Manual-ID traces, model identity/quota/dimensions and private DB access    Question queued  Outbox, queue, worker and ScaledObject; check sender/scaler/receiver roles separately    Question processing/failed  Worker request-ID logs, model throttling, lock renewal and deadline    Wrong evidence  Product filter, stored chunks, retrieval count and prompt    
 Function logs:   function-logs.kql   in Application Insights. Failure stores are separate: Event Grid's  event-deadletters  blobs, Function host's  webjobs-blobtrigger-poison , and Service Bus  $DeadLetterQueue . Do not dump webhook destination URLs; they contain a system key. 
 
 Clean up 
   Bash · repository root  Copy    bash workshop/scripts/cleanup.sh
    Canonical commands:   commands.sh   
 The tool verifies the tagged workshop group, lists resources and requires  DELETE  plus its full name. After submission, run the printed  az group exists  check until false; confirm AKS's managed node group is also gone. Deletion may be blocked by locks/policy. 
  Soft delete and local cleanup  Key Vault has seven-day soft-delete retention; App Configuration one day. No purge is performed, so names may remain reserved. Provider registrations remain. Remove local  workshop/.state  only after Azure cleanup is confirmed.  
 You have exercised 
 Docker/ACR, AKS manifests/probes/rollouts, Flyway + pgvector, Blob/Event Grid/Functions, Service Bus request/reply, identity/configuration/secrets, grounded RAG and KEDA scaling. 
 For your first run:  walkthrough checklist . For production changes, indexing or additional exam coverage:  reference notes .

title: Versions, decisions and sources
summary: Architecture decisions, selected exam objectives, costs and official documentation.
text:
Implementation decisions 
 The core deliberately favors explicit code: Java 21, supported Spring Boot, Maven Wrapper, JdbcClient/SQL, Thymeleaf and Flyway; Python 3.12, direct Azure SDK clients and small HTTP model calls; PostgreSQL 17 and an exact pgvector cosine scan. Application source is maintained in  Products ,  ProductsEmbedder  and  ProductsChat . The two Python repositories vendor the same small rag_core package; the integration checks compare them. 
 PostgreSQL is private to the VNet, with a delegated subnet and private DNS. AKS and Functions use explicit NAT egress for public, identity-protected Azure endpoints. Storage containers are private and shared-key access is disabled. This core avoids private endpoints for every service and avoids a multi-day network/security course. 
 One database owner is used by migrations and applications, and TLS  sslmode=require  encrypts PostgreSQL traffic inside the private network. Production should separate runtime/migration roles and use full certificate/hostname verification appropriate to its trust store. The Products endpoint has self-signed HTTPS, a source-IP restriction and a random password. It is not public anonymous HTTP, nor a production SSO implementation. 
 Application settings/secrets are read only on startup. Workers are serial with prefetch zero. Messaging is at-least-once with explicit idempotency. Model calls have finite connect/read timeouts; request deadlines and failure states persist independently of the browser. 
 
  Version and dependency matrix 
   VERSIONS.md   records the exact direct versions, image tags, API versions and validation-tool versions.   constraints.txt   locks the resolved Python dependency versions; it constrains only packages that each requirements file actually installs. The Maven parent and Azure BOM manage Java dependency versions. 
    Component  Selected baseline      Java / application framework  Java 21; Spring Boot 4.1.2; Maven Wrapper 3.3.4 / Maven 3.9.11    Python  3.12 in the Function and worker; dependencies pinned in canonical requirements + constraints    Data  PostgreSQL 17; SQL extension vector;  vector(1536) ; exact cosine query    Function  Functions v4, Python v2 programming model, 4.x extension bundle, Flex Consumption FC1, managed-identity deployment storage    Models  gpt-5-mini / 2025-08-07 and text-embedding-3-small / 1; Azure OpenAI GA v1 REST endpoints; GlobalStandard SKU    Kubernetes  AKS-supported default version at creation, patch upgrades; bundled KEDA add-on. Check kubectl minor-version skew after deployment.    
 
  Selected AI-200 objectives 
 Checked against the  official AI-200 study guide  on  11 November 2026 , for the skills dated 7 October 2026. This is a partial exercise mapping, not a coverage guarantee. 
    Exercise  Relevant objective area  Boundary      Build, tag and push  Container images and ACR  Local Docker builds; ACR Tasks is not implemented    Manifests, probes, logs, rollout  AKS deployment and troubleshooting  No Container Apps revisions or App Service deployment    KEDA queue scaling  Event-driven scaling concepts  The guide's KEDA objective names Container Apps; this exercise uses AKS    Flyway, explicit SQL, vectors  PostgreSQL data modeling, queries and RAG with metadata filters  Small exact scans; advanced index tuning is optional    Request/reply and failures  Service Bus processing and dead letters  Queues, not a full topics/subscriptions lab    Blob notification and Function  Event Grid workflows and Function configuration/deployment  Blob triggers, not a general Functions API course    Secrets and ordinary settings  Key Vault retrieval and App Configuration  No automatic rotation/live refresh claim    Inspect Function traces  KQL/log troubleshooting practice  No complete distributed OpenTelemetry instrumentation    
 Cosmos DB, Managed Redis, Container Apps/App Service specifics and broader monitoring work remain outside this workshop. Blob Storage and basic model calls support the application; their presence does not make every related service feature a measured exercise. 
 
  Cost drivers and cleanup 
 The four-hour US$5–15 planning allowance is intentionally approximate. It assumes one small node, a Burstable database, a few manuals, at most a handful of bounded eight-question demos, and prompt deletion. No bill has been measured for this implementation. Regional capacity, pricing agreements, minimum billing units and model token usage change the result. 
   Persistent until deletion:  AKS node/disks, database compute/storage, NAT/public IPs, ACR, Service Bus and App Configuration. Scaling the chat worker to zero does not remove these costs.   Usage-based:  model tokens, Function execution, storage operations/data transfer and log ingestion. Restrict repeated load runs; failed/retried model calls can also cost tokens.   After cleanup:  confirm ARM deletion and AKS's node-group removal. Soft-deleted Key Vault/App Configuration names remain subject to their recovery/retention behavior.  
 Use  Azure Pricing Calculator ,  AKS pricing ,  PostgreSQL pricing  and  Azure model pricing  before your own run. Budget alerts notify; they are not a hard spending cap. 
 
  Official documentation used 
 Local setup instructions checked 11 November 2026:  WinGet installation flags ,  Docker Desktop package manifest ,  WSL installation commands ,  Docker Desktop requirements and licensing ,  Docker WSL integration ,  Azure CLI apt repository  and  kubectl download/checksum verification . 
 The following references were checked on 11 November 2026. Script compilation/local tests and live Azure acceptance are different forms of evidence; see the validation report. 
   Spring Boot requirements  and  Maven Wrapper .   AKS workload identity  and  KEDA add-on/operator identity configuration .   Flex Consumption hosting and trigger constraints ,  Function infrastructure/deployment storage , and  CLI deployment and VNet integration .   Event Grid-backed Blob trigger webhook  and  Function host/binding identity requirements .   PostgreSQL private networking/DNS ,  Extension allowlisting , and  pgvector's operators and dimension types .   Azure OpenAI GA v1 chat REST contract ,  Model quota  and  Model retirement schedule .   Service Bus locks and settlement ,  Dead-letter handling , and  KEDA Service Bus scaler settings .

title: First-run walkthrough checklist
summary: A maintainer acceptance path with expected outcomes and diagnostics.
text:
Before the first Azure run 
 This is a participant-path checklist, not an instructor timetable. Record actual outcomes, elapsed time, region, selected versions and fixes. The proposed core duration is an estimate until a person follows it successfully. 
  Build the static site with  python scripts/build.py . Serve the repository at the documented base path and follow the workshop link from the main page. Check navigation, copy, search, source viewer, theme and persisted completion/reset.  Use a clean, suitable subscription scope or a fresh workshop prefix. Run prerequisite checks without bypassing missing permissions or quota. Confirm the actual selected subscription with the owner.  Review the cost estimate, create only the model stage, and require the actual identity-based embedding/chat probe to pass before AKS/database provisioning starts.  Start stage 02, then perform the Docker chapter while provisioning runs. Record whether this overlap is enough to keep the main path near four hours.  Wait through stage 03. Verify the VM is Ready, Functions is on Flex/Python 3.12, PostgreSQL has private networking and VECTOR is allowlisted. No internet-wide database firewall rule should exist.  Complete roles/settings/federation. Inspect the KEDA operator's identity separately, and confirm the kubelet can pull both image tags.  
 
  Core acceptance observations 
    Step  Expected outcome  Useful diagnostic      Products rollout  Ready Pod, Flyway version 1, signed-in upload/chat pages over restricted HTTPS   kubectl describe pod -n products -l app=products ; Products logs    New manual  Waiting/processing → ready; nonzero unique chunks, 1536 dimensions   bash workshop/scripts/inspect-data.sh ; Function manual-ID trace    Duplicate event  No extra chunk rows or changed ready data   python workshop/tools/replay_event.py , then compare counts    Known question  Queued/processing → completed; correct correlation and relevant product/manual references  Request ID in worker/Products logs and PostgreSQL state    Unsupported question  Explicit insufficient information, no invented specification  Read actual retrieved passages and model instruction    Retrieval setting  After worker restart, new request uses count=1; restore 3  Worker startup log and at most one returned citation    KEDA cycle  0 → backlog → 1 → more than 1 → completed answers → 0; Products stays 1  Observer output, ScaledObject/HPA conditions, model throttle logs    Real smoke  Pass with source IDs and temperature evidence, without exact answer assertion   .state/smoke-result.json ; bounded timeout diagnostic    Cleanup  Workshop group and managed AKS node group gone; retention explained  Printed  az group exists  command and cost/resource view    
 
  Reproduce local software checks 
   verify-local.sh   runs local verification with a disposable loopback-only PostgreSQL/pgvector container and removes that container on exit. It requires Java 21, Docker and Python 3.12+. Its model fixtures are deterministic: passing them does not demonstrate Azure identity or live model behavior. 
 Run  bash workshop/scripts/verify-local.sh . Use  python -m playwright install chromium  inside the verification environment before the browser suite, or set  BROWSER_EXECUTABLE  to a compatible installed Chromium/Edge executable. The browser tests run at  /ai200/workshop/ , not only at the host root. 
 For infrastructure, compile all four Bicep files with  for file in workshop/infra/*.bicep; do az bicep build --file "$file" --stdout > /dev/null; done  and perform ARM/server-side validation in the intended subscription before a clean deployment. Run  bash -n  and ShellCheck on the scripts. Validate rendered standard manifests against Kubernetes schemas and KEDA resources against the official add-on CRDs; then validate against the actual cluster with  kubectl apply --dry-run=server  before applying. 
 The supplied  python workshop/tools/validate_manifests.py  creates non-secret fixture renderings and validates the custom resources against official KEDA 2.18.2 CRDs. Standard resources can be checked with the pinned kubeconform container, as reproduced in the repository's workshop-checks workflow. These offline structures do not prove live cluster admission, current Azure capacity or identity propagation. 
 
  Record what actually happened 
 Update   VALIDATION.md   with command summaries and dates. Separate local fixture results, container results, ARM/schema checks, live model probes and the actual deployment smoke result. Do not turn “expected output” from a chapter into an observed result. Record any Azure blocker explicitly and leave its acceptance row unverified. 
 If the path takes substantially longer than four hours after prerequisites, record the slow chapters. Keep advanced indexing, identity hardening and production operations optional; do not remove the requested core learning goals just to claim a shorter duration.

title: Validation report
summary: Observed local checks and Azure-specific checks still required.
text:
Observed software checks 
 Full results:   VALIDATION.md  . Local model tests use deterministic fixtures. 
  Local test coverage and outcomes 
 Java compilation, Flyway migration/rerun, product commit ordering, persistent outbox, correlation, duplicate replies and timeout persistence have been checked against real PostgreSQL. Python core tests cover chunking, duplicate indexing, vector dimensions, failure/retry persistence, filtered retrieval, result caching and binding metadata. Direct Python dependency resolution and Bicep compilation have also been performed. 
  Observed:  four Java integration tests, 26 workshop pytest cases, all 58 existing Python tests and 91 existing JavaScript tests pass. Both Linux container images build; the Products inspect container's actual HTTP health is UP. Real browser checks, shell lint, strict standard Kubernetes schemas and official KEDA CRD structures pass. The canonical report describes the fixture boundaries and commands. 
  Interface/setup follow-up:  14 relevant checks pass after adopting the default header and shared jargon tooltips: five browser, six documentation/export and three local-preflight boundary cases. The 58 existing Python and 91 JavaScript checks were rerun successfully. Windows setup parsing and a real  -WhatIf  preview, Ubuntu Bash syntax and ShellCheck pass. A clean OS installation using the new installers has not been run; no local software was installed or changed for this verification. 
 
 What still needs Azure 
   Azure testing is deliberately left for the user's walkthrough.  No providers were registered or paid resources created. Read-only checks found Compute, AKS and model providers unregistered and regional quota queries empty; empty results do not prove a lack of quota. Use the supplied registration/check stage in the intended subscription first.  
  Remaining cloud checks  Actual cloud model probes, ARM/server-side validation, a clean deployment, Function host/Event Grid delivery, private-network access, workload/KEDA identity propagation, public HTTPS access, the real smoke test, observed scaling and cloud cleanup require the maintainer acceptance path in a suitable authorized subscription.  
  How to interpret the tutorial 
 Chapter outputs are expected behavior unless explicitly recorded as observed in the dated report. The core path is estimated at about four hours after tools/access are ready. It has not been timed with a participant. Fix and record first-run failures rather than converting expectations into a claim of success.
